context.content: Hey guys, ​ I'm a 25 year old, former nurse, currently a 3rd year medical student, living in Portugal with portuguese citizenship. No debt to my name. Working since 16 yo, living frugaly so I don't have to ask my parents for help or dip into my savings until i finish medschool. Have 7k in an emergency fund and around 6-7k in an insurance type of saving account. Currently the universities are on remote learning due to covid and I'm hopping back in my nursing uniform to help out in the local ICU starting next week. I'm thinking that the current school year is going to go to shit, so I'll end up working all up until september. I'm looking to invest some of my future earnings (around 3k) into something for 3-5 years and keep around 500 euros to invest in shares, but I don't want to end up in /r/wallstreetbets and cry about my losses, I want to do it the smart way. ​ I'm asking you guys for learning material, as my financial literacy is not the greatest, I just track my spendings and save as much as possible but that's obviously not going to help much. I roamed about the sub and found a couple of useful links, but the information is hella scattered, so If anyone could hook me up with links and suggestions, I'd be very thankful. ​ What is the best program to use? So far I've looked into Degiro and Trader 212, lets suppose I want to invest my 300-500 into shares asap and over the months start getting into bonds. Is trader 212 the way to go? ​ Does anyone have a document on how are dividends and sold shares taxed in portugal? I've been lurking around the government website but can't seem to find it. ​ What ETFs would be the best to put my money on? VWCE and chill? ​ Anything else is also greatly appreciated
